Looking at the quotation, the specific mechanism named is a coordinated set of government policy strategies targeting child welfare, poverty, education, and social care — all aimed at improving outcomes for children and young people.

The quotation explicitly names: a child poverty strategy, a best start in life strategy, children's social care reform, a schools white paper, and a post-16 white paper. The overarching framing is about child well-being and growing up — not a single instrument but a coordinated policy agenda for children.

The dominant theme is child poverty and well-being strategies (child poverty strategy, best start in life), with education as one component. The unifying goal is child welfare/well-being outcomes.

I38 — Government Policy • Provision and Effects of Welfare Programs fits well as the coordinated government welfare/poverty/social care policy agenda. But I28 (Government Policy in Education) also fits the schools and post-16 elements.

The primary thrust is the integrated child welfare and poverty strategy — making this the best country to grow up in — which maps most precisely to I38.
